title: Your capstone action, your case story and your 90-day plan

say: Your capstone action, your case story, and your 90-day plan.
This is the video for module 4 of Client Relationship Management.
Your capstone proves you can manage client relationships, not just describe them. It starts with a working tracker, and one proactive action you took with a real client, with her response.

panel.heading: Prove it with real evidence
items: A working tracker with real client history
One proactive action and the client's reply
A case story with honest numbers
A 90-day plan and a weekly routine

say: Then you turn that work into a short case story with numbers, and finish with a 90-day plan, so the habits continue after the course.

say: Choose a Re-engage or Grow client from your monthly review, and read her notes first.
A weak message just asks for work.

say: A value-first message gives her something useful and specific, based on what she told you. You mentioned your shop anniversary is on 15 July. Would branded gift packs help?
This is why the records matter.

say: Then she asks Grace if she may use this exchange in her course project, without her name. Grace agrees.
Not every action leads to an order. Record exactly what happened. An honest no order yet is better evidence than an invented success.

say: Before you use any client's messages, ask her permission, even with her name hidden.
Blur names, phone numbers, profile photos and addresses in every screenshot, and call her Client A in your summary.
Share a copy or screenshot of your tracker, never the live file.

panel.heading: Protect privacy in your evidence
items: Ask the client's permission first
Blur names, numbers, photos and addresses
Call her "Client A" in your summary
Never share your live tracker file

say: Saying I am good with clients proves nothing. Everyone says it. A short case story with real numbers convinces people.

panel.heading: Situation, Action, Result
items: Situation: the problem, with a number
Action: exactly what you did
Result: before and after, with dates

say: Situation. For example, Funmi had 46 clients, but no record of who had stopped buying.

panel.heading: Situation, Action, Result
items: Situation: the problem, with a number
Action: exactly what you did
Result: before and after, with dates

say: Action. She built a Google Sheets tracker, set reorder reminders from each client's buying gap, and started day-3 after-care checks.

panel.heading: Situation, Action, Result
items: Situation: the problem, with a number
Action: exactly what you did
Result: before and after, with dates

say: Result. Her retention went from 82.5 percent to about 89 percent the next quarter.
She tells it three ways. For an employer, the numbers. For a partner, her reliability. For a shop client, simply: I remind you before you run out.

say: Relationship management is a routine, not a project you finish. Block 30 minutes in your calendar every week. Open the tracker and act on every red row.

panel.heading: The weekly 30-minute routine
items: Clear the red rows
Log this week's orders
Check promises due in seven days
Send after-care checks
Send reorder reminders

say: Your plan names one relationship to deepen. For example, Zainab in Kaduna chooses Blessing, a valuable client who went quiet.

cards.d: Blessing, a high-value Re-engage client: a voice note in week 1, then a fixed fortnightly slot.
Day-3 after-care for every client, and reorder reminders 5 days before each usual gap ends.
By 31 December: retention 75 percent or more, and at least 3 new referred clients.

say: It names a rhythm she will keep: after-care on day 3 for every client, and reminders 5 days before each client's usual gap ends.

cards.d: Blessing, a high-value Re-engage client: a voice note in week 1, then a fixed fortnightly slot.
Day-3 after-care for every client, and reorder reminders 5 days before each usual gap ends.
By 31 December: retention 75 percent or more, and at least 3 new referred clients.

say: And it sets modest targets from her baseline of 70 percent retention: 75 percent or more by 31 December, and at least 3 new referred clients.
Anyone could check on 31 December whether she did it. Share your plan with one person who will check on you.

say: To remember. Give value first, using what you know about her. Protect her privacy in your evidence. Tell your story as Situation, Action, Result, with honest numbers. Keep your weekly 30 minutes. And make your 90-day plan specific enough to check.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Start outreach from her notes, give value first
Ask permission and hide every identifying detail
Situation, Action, Result, with real numbers
Block a weekly 30-minute review
One relationship, one rhythm, 2 to 3 targets

say: Now practise. Take one value-first action with a real client and save privacy-safe evidence. Write your case story for an employer and a client. Then write your 90-day plan, book your weekly review, and re-take the ten-point audit.
